name: ATR 42
facts: Its name comes from its seat count: the original seated around 42 passengers.
family_comparison: The shortest member of the ATR family, 4.5 m shorter than the ATR 72.

name: ATR 72
facts: You usually board at the back: the cargo hold and its door are at the front.

photo.author: Laurent ERRERA from L'Union, France, derivative work Lämpel

name: Airbus A220-100
facts: Bombardier designed it as the CSeries. It became an Airbus in 2018.

name: Airbus A220-300
facts: Its windows are among the largest of any single-aisle jet.
family_comparison: The longest member of the A220 family, 3.7 m longer than the A220-100.

photo.author: Steve Lynes from Sandshurst, United Kingdom

name: Airbus A318
facts: British Airways flew it with 32 business-class seats from London City to New York. The runway was too short to take off with full tanks, so it stopped in Shannon to refuel.
family_comparison: The shortest member of the A320 family, 6.1 m shorter than the A320.

name: Airbus A319
facts: Easy to tell from an A320: it has one emergency exit over each wing instead of two.
family_comparison: It's 3.7 m shorter than the A320.

name: Airbus A319neo
facts: One of the rarest Airbus jets flying today: airlines ordered far more A320neos and A321neos.
family_comparison: It's 3.7 m shorter than the A320.

name: Airbus A320
facts: The first airliner with digital fly-by-wire controls: pilots fly it with a sidestick, not a yoke.

name: Airbus A320neo
facts: “neo” stands for New Engine Option. Its bigger engines burn up to 20% less fuel per seat than the original A320.

name: Airbus A321
facts: The first Airbus to be assembled in Hamburg rather than Toulouse.
family_comparison: The longest member of the A320 family, 6.9 m longer than the A320.

name: Airbus A321neo
facts: Its long-range versions, the A321LR and XLR, carry passengers across the Atlantic in a single-aisle jet.
family_comparison: The longest member of the A320 family, 6.9 m longer than the A320.

name: Airbus A330-200
facts: Air forces turned it into the A330 MRTT, a tanker that refuels fighter jets in flight.
family_comparison: It's 4.8 m shorter than the A330-300.

name: Airbus A330-300
facts: Airbus designed it alongside the four-engined A340. The two share the same wing and cockpit.

name: Airbus A330-800
facts: The longest-range A330, able to fly up to 15,000 km nonstop.
family_comparison: It's 4.8 m shorter than the A330-300.

name: Airbus A330-900
facts: Its curved wingtips, inspired by the A350's, add 3.7 m to the wingspan of the original A330.

name: Airbus A340-300
facts: Its four engines let it fly the most direct routes over oceans, at a time when twin-engine jets still had to stay within a set flying time of an airport.

photo.author: Laurent ERRERA from L'Union, France, derivative work Lämpel

name: Airbus A340-600
facts: It was the longest airliner in the world until the Boeing 747-8 arrived.
family_comparison: It's 11.7 m longer than the A340-300.

name: Airbus A350-1000
facts: Qantas picked it for Project Sunrise: nonstop flights from Sydney to London and New York.
family_comparison: The longest member of the A350 family, 7 m longer than the A350-900.

name: Airbus A350-900
facts: More than half of its structure is carbon-fibre composite rather than aluminium.

name: Airbus A380
facts: The largest passenger airliner ever built, with two full-length decks. It is certified for up to 853 passengers, though airlines fit around 500 to 600.

name: Antonov An-24
facts: More than 60 years after its first flight, it still carries passengers on scheduled routes in Siberia.

name: Boeing 717
facts: McDonnell Douglas designed it as the MD-95. It got its Boeing name after the two companies merged in 1997.

name: Boeing 737 MAX 10
facts: Its main landing gear stretches on take-off, so the long tail stays clear of the runway.
family_comparison: The longest member of the 737 MAX family, 4.3 m longer than the 737 MAX 8.

photo.author: Steve Knight from Halstead, United Kingdom

name: Boeing 737 MAX 7
facts: The longest-range MAX: its shorter cabin leaves more of the weight allowance for fuel.
family_comparison: The shortest member of the 737 MAX family, 3.9 m shorter than the 737 MAX 8.

photo.author: Steve Lynes from Sandshurst, United Kingdom

name: Boeing 737 MAX 8
facts: Its split-tip winglets point both up and down.

name: Boeing 737 MAX 9
facts: It can seat up to 220 passengers, about as many as the larger Boeing 757-200.
family_comparison: It's 2.6 m longer than the 737 MAX 8.

photo.author: Clemens Vasters from Viersen, Germany, Germany

name: Boeing 737-700
facts: Boeing's first business jet, the BBJ, is a 737-700 fitted with the stronger wing of the 737-800.
family_comparison: It's 5.9 m shorter than the 737-800.

name: Boeing 737-800
facts: The best-selling 737 before the MAX, with almost 5,000 built.

name: Boeing 737-900ER
facts: To carry up to 220 passengers, it needed an extra pair of emergency exits behind the wing.
family_comparison: It's 2.6 m longer than the 737-800.

name: Boeing 747-400
facts: It was the first 747 flown by two pilots: a new digital cockpit replaced the flight engineer.

photo.author: Luis Argerich from Buenos Aires, Argentina

name: Boeing 747-8
facts: When it entered service in 2012, it was the longest airliner in the world, 3.5 m longer than the A380.
family_comparison: It's 5.6 m longer than the 747-400.

name: Boeing 757-200
facts: Production ended in 2004, yet it still flies across the Atlantic every day.

photo.author: Dylan Ashe from San Jose, USA

name: Boeing 757-300
facts: The longest single-aisle twinjet ever built.
family_comparison: The longest member of the 757 family, 7.1 m longer than the 757-200.

name: Boeing 767-300ER
facts: In 1985 the 767 opened the Atlantic to twin-engine jets, which until then had to stay close to an airport.

name: Boeing 767-400ER
facts: Only two airlines ordered it new: Delta and Continental, which is now part of United.
family_comparison: It's 6.4 m longer than the 767-300ER.

name: Boeing 777-200ER
facts: The 777 was the first airliner designed entirely on computer, without a full-size mock-up.

name: Boeing 777-200LR
facts: In 2005 it flew 21,602 km nonstop from Hong Kong to London the long way round, over the Pacific: an airliner record.

name: Boeing 777-300
facts: Japanese airlines flew it on busy domestic routes with more than 500 seats.
family_comparison: It's 10.1 m longer than the 777-200ER.

name: Boeing 777-300ER
facts: Its GE90-115B is one of the most powerful jet engines ever certified, at over 115,000 lbf of thrust.
family_comparison: It's 10.1 m longer than the 777-200ER.

name: Boeing 777-9
facts: Its wingtips fold up at the gate, so it fits the same airport stands as a 777-300ER.
At 76.7 m, the longest airliner ever built, just ahead of the 747-8.
family_comparison: It's 13 m longer than the 777-200ER.

photo.author: Tomás Del Coro from Fabulous Las Vegas, Nevada, USA

name: Boeing 787-10
facts: Singapore Airlines was the first to fly it, in 2018.
family_comparison: The longest member of the 787 family, 11.6 m longer than the 787-8.

name: Boeing 787-8
facts: The cabin is pressurised to the equivalent of 6,000 ft instead of the usual 8,000, so you land less tired.

name: Boeing 787-9
facts: Qantas flies it nonstop between Perth and London, in about 17 hours.
family_comparison: It's 6.1 m longer than the 787-8.

photo.author: Gordon Werner from Seattle, United States, derivative work Lämpel

name: Bombardier CRJ1000
facts: The largest CRJ ever built. Spain's Air Nostrum flies more of them than any other airline.
family_comparison: It's 6.8 m longer than the CRJ700.

name: Bombardier CRJ200
facts: Its overhead bins are too small for most roller bags, so yours is often taken at the aircraft door and handed back on arrival.
family_comparison: It's 5.5 m shorter than the CRJ700.

name: Bombardier CRJ700
facts: The CRJ line grew out of a business jet, the Canadair Challenger.

name: Bombardier CRJ900
facts: Mitsubishi bought the CRJ programme in 2020, and production ended that same year.
family_comparison: It's 3.9 m longer than the CRJ700.

photo.author: Clive R Martin from Addlestone Surrey, England

name: COMAC C909
facts: Known as the ARJ21 until 2024, it was the first Chinese-designed jet airliner to carry passengers.

name: COMAC C919
facts: China's first home-grown mainline airliner, flying passengers with China Eastern since 2023.

name: De Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter
facts: On Scotland's Isle of Barra, Loganair lands it on a beach, and the timetable follows the tide.

name: De Havilland Canada Dash 8-100/200
facts: Norway's Widerøe flies it into local airports whose runways are only about 800 m long.

name: De Havilland Canada Dash 8-300
facts: From 1996 Dash 8s got active cabin noise suppression, and a Q for “quiet” in their name.
family_comparison: It's 3.4 m longer than the Dash 8-100/200.

name: De Havilland Canada Dash 8-400
facts: One of the fastest turboprop airliners, cruising at around 660 km/h.
family_comparison: The longest member of the Dash 8 family, 10.6 m longer than the Dash 8-100/200.

name: Embraer 170
facts: Built in São José dos Campos, Brazil, the city where Embraer was founded in 1969.

name: Embraer 175
facts: The workhorse of US regional flights: pilot contracts cap regional jets at 76 seats, and it fits exactly.
family_comparison: It's 1.8 m longer than the E170.

name: Embraer 190
facts: No middle seats: like every E-Jet, its cabin is laid out two by two.
family_comparison: It's 6.3 m longer than the E170.

name: Embraer 195
facts: Azul, the Brazilian airline founded by JetBlue's founder David Neeleman, built its network on the E195.
family_comparison: The longest member of the E-Jet family, 8.8 m longer than the E170.

name: Embraer E190-E2
facts: A new wing and geared turbofan engines cut its fuel burn by about 17% compared with the first E190.

name: Embraer E195-E2
facts: The largest airliner Embraer has ever built.
family_comparison: It's 5.4 m longer than the E190-E2.

name: Embraer ERJ 145
facts: Its seats are laid out one and two, so most passengers get either a window or an aisle.

name: Fokker 100
facts: Fokker went bankrupt in 1996, yet Australia's Alliance Airlines still flies a large fleet of them.

name: Let L-410 Turbolet
facts: It flies into Lukla, the gateway to Everest, where the sloping runway is just 527 m long.

name: Saab 340
facts: Saab, also known for fighter jets and once for cars, first developed it with America's Fairchild.

name: Sukhoi Superjet 100
facts: The first all-new Russian airliner since the fall of the Soviet Union.
